nodes.name: Lebesgue conditional expectation
nodes.statement: {} The {\bf conditional expectation} of a $\mathcal X$-measurable function $f : X \to [0, \infty]$ is \[\mu[f | \mathcal B] = ??\]
nodes.label: def:lebesgue-cond-exp

nodes.name: Characterisation of the Lebesgue conditional expectation
nodes.statement: {} If $f : X \to [0, \infty]$ is a $\mathcal X$-measurable function, then $\mu[f | \mathcal B]$ is the $\mu$-ae unique $\mathcal B$-measurable function $X \to [0, \infty]$ such that \[\int_B \mu[f | \mathcal B]\ \partial\mu = \int_B f\ \partial\mu\] for all $B \in \mathcal B$.
nodes.label: lem:lebesgue-cond-exp-char

nodes.statement: Standard machine.

nodes.name: Juxtaposition
nodes.statement: {} Let $E$ and $S$ be sets. Let $\Delta\in\mathcal{P}(S)$, and let $\omega\in E^S$. We define \begin{align} \mathrm{Juxt}_{\omega} : E^\Delta&\to E^S\\ \zeta&\mapsto \delta\mapsto\begin{cases} \zeta_\delta & \delta\in\Delta\\ \omega_\delta & \delta\notin\Delta \end{cases} \end{align} to be the \textbf{juxtaposition of $\zeta$ and $\omega$} (for each $\zeta\in E^\Delta$).
nodes.label: def:juxtaposition

nodes.name: Cylinder events
nodes.statement: {} Let $(E,\mathcal{E})$ be a measurable space, and let $S$ be a set. Then, \begin{align} \mathcal{F}:\mathcal{P}(S)&\to \left\{ \text{sigma algebras on } E^S \right\}\\ \Delta&\mapsto \sigma(\{\text{proj}_\delta:E^S\to E\mid \delta\in \Delta\}) \end{align} defines the \textbf{cylinder events in }$\Delta$ (for each $\Delta\in\mathcal{P}(S)$), where each $\text{proj}_\delta$ is the coordinate projection at coordinate $\delta$.
nodes.label: def:cylinder-event

nodes.name: Kernel
nodes.statement: {} Let $(X,\mathcal X)$ and $(Y,\mathcal{Y})$ be measurable spaces. Then, \[\text{Ker}_{\mathcal{Y},\mathcal X}:=\left\{\pi:\mathcal X\times Y\to[0,\infty]~\middle\vert~ \forall y\in Y,\pi(\cdot\mid y)\in\mathfrak{M}(X,\mathcal X);~\forall A\in\mathcal X,\pi(A\mid\cdot)\text{ is }\mathcal{Y}\text{-measurable}\right\}\] defines the set of \textbf{kernels from $\mathcal{Y}$ to $\mathcal X$}, where $\mathfrak{M}(X,\mathcal X)$ is the space of measures on $X$.
nodes.label: def:kernel

nodes.name: Markov kernel
nodes.statement: {} Let $(X,\mathcal X)$ and $(Y,\mathcal{Y})$ be measurable spaces. We say that $\pi\in\text{Ker}_{\mathcal{Y},\mathcal X}$ is a \textbf{Markov kernel} iff $\pi(X\mid \cdot)=1$.
nodes.label: def:markov-ker

nodes.name: Proper kernel
nodes.statement: {} $\pi$ is \textbf{proper} iff $\pi(A\cap B\mid x)=\pi(A\mid x)\cdot\mathbf{1}_B(x)$ for all $A\in\mathcal X$, $B\in\mathcal B$ and $x\in X$.
nodes.label: def:proper-ker

nodes.name: Lebesgue integral characterisation of proper kernels
nodes.statement: {} If $\pi$ is proper, then \[\int f(x) g(x)\ \pi(dx\mid x_0) = g(x_0)\int f(x)\ \pi(dx\mid x_0)\] for all $x_0 \in X$ and functions $f, g : X \to [0, \infty]$ such that $f$ is $\mathcal X$-measurable, $g$ is $\mathcal B$-measurable.
nodes.label: lem:proper-ker-lintegral

nodes.statement: {} Standard machine.

nodes.name: Integral characterisation of proper kernels
nodes.statement: {} If $\pi$ is a proper Markov kernel and $g$ is a bounded function, then \[\int f(x) g(x)\ \pi(dx\mid x_0) = g(x_0)\int f(x)\ \pi(dx\mid x_0)\] for all $x_0 \in X$ and functions $f, g : X \to \mathbb R$ such that $f$ is bounded $\mathcal X$-measurable and $g$ is bounded $\mathcal B$-measurable.
nodes.label: lem:proper-ker-integral

nodes.statement: Standard machine.

nodes.name: Conditional expectation kernel
nodes.statement: {} Let $\mu\in\mathfrak{M}(X,\mathcal X)$. Then, $\pi\in\text{Ker}_{\mathcal B,\mathcal X}$ is a \textbf{conditional expectation kernel for $\mu$} if $\mu(A\mid \mathcal B)=\pi(A\mid\cdot)$ $\mu$-a.e.
nodes.label: def:cond-exp-ker

nodes.name: Lebesgue integral characterisation of proper conditional expectation kernels
nodes.statement: If $\pi \in \text{Ker}_{\mathcal B, \mathcal X}$ is a conditional expectation kernel for $\mu$, then \[\mu[f\mid \mathcal B] = \int f(x)\ \pi(\partial x\mid\cdot)\ \mu\text{-a.e.}\] for all $\mathcal X$-measurable functions $f : X \to [0, \infty]$.
nodes.label: lem:cond-exp-proper-ker-lintegral

nodes.statement: Standard machine.

nodes.name: Integral characterisation of proper conditional expectation kernels
nodes.statement: If $\pi \in \text{Ker}_{\mathcal B, \mathcal X}$ is a conditional expectation kernel for $\mu$, then $$\mu(f\mid \mathcal B) = \int f(x)\ \pi(\partial x\mid\cdot)\ \mu\text{-a.e.}$$ for all bounded $\mathcal X$-measurable functions $f : X \to \mathbb R$.
nodes.label: lem:cond-exp-proper-ker-integral

nodes.statement: Standard machine.

nodes.name: Characterisation of proper conditional expectation kernels, Remark 1.20
nodes.statement: Let $\mu\in\mathfrak{M}(X,\mathcal X)$ be a finite measure and let $\pi\in\text{Ker}_{\mathcal B,\mathcal X}$ be a proper kernel. Then, $$\pi \text{ is a conditional expectation kernel for }\mu \iff \mu\pi = \mu$$
nodes.label: lem:cond-exp-proper-ker-bind

nodes.statement: By the characterisation of conditional expectation, $$\pi \text{ is a conditional expectation kernel for }\mu \iff \forall A \in \mathcal X, \forall B \in \mathcal B, \mu(A \cap B) = \int_B \pi(A|\cdot)\ \partial\mu$$ By properness of $\pi$, $$\int_B \pi(A|\cdot)\ \partial\mu = \mu\pi(A \cap B)$$ Hence \begin{align} \pi \text{ is a cond. exp. kernel with respect to }\mu & \iff \forall A \in \mathcal X, \forall B \in \mathcal B, \mu(A \cap B) = \mu\pi(A \cap B) \\ & \iff \forall A \in \mathcal X, \mu(A) = \mu\pi(A) \\ & \iff \mu = \mu\pi \end{align}

nodes.name: Specification
nodes.statement: {} A {\bf specification} is a family of kernels $\gamma : \mathrm{Finset} S \to \mathrm{Ker}_{\mathcal{F}_{S\setminus\Lambda}, \mathcal{E}^S}$ which is {\bf consistent}, in the sense that \[\forall \Lambda_1, \Lambda_2 \in \mathrm{Finset}(S), \Lambda_1 \subseteq \Lambda_2 \implies \gamma_{\Lambda_1} \circ_k \gamma_{\Lambda_2} = \gamma_{\Lambda_2}\]
nodes.label: def:spec

nodes.name: Independent specification
nodes.statement: {} A specification $\gamma$ is \textbf{independent} iff \[\forall \Lambda_1, \Lambda_2 \in \mathrm{Finset}(S), \gamma_{\Lambda_1} \circ_k \gamma_{\Lambda_2} = \gamma_{\Lambda_1\cup\Lambda_2}\]
nodes.label: def:indep-spec

nodes.name: Markov specification
nodes.statement: {} A specification $\gamma$ is a \textbf{Markov specification} iff $\gamma_\Lambda$ is a probability kernel for every $\Lambda \in \mathrm{Finset}(S)$.
nodes.label: def:markov-spec

nodes.name: Proper specification
nodes.statement: {} A specification $\gamma$ is \textbf{proper} iff the kernel $\gamma_\Lambda$ is proper for every $\Lambda \in \mathrm{Finset}(S)$.
nodes.label: def:proper-spec

nodes.name: Gibbs measures
nodes.statement: Given a specification $\gamma$, a \textbf{Gibbs measures specified by $\gamma$} is a measure $\nu \in \mathfrak{M}(E^S, \mathcal{E}^S)$ such that $\gamma_\Lambda(A|\cdot)$ is a conditional expectation kernel for $\nu$ for all $A \in \mathcal E^S$ and $\Lambda \in \mathrm{Finset}(S)$.
nodes.label: def:gibbs-meas

nodes.name: Product probability measure
nodes.statement: {} Let $I$ be a set. Suppose for each $i\in I$ that $(\Omega_i,\mathcal B_i,P_i)$ is a probability space. Then, $P:=\bigotimes_{i\in I}P_i$ is a well-defined product probability measure on $\prod_{i\in I}\Omega_i$.

nodes.name: Modifier
nodes.statement: {} A {\bf modifier of $\gamma$} is a family \[\rho : \mathrm{Finset}(S) \to \Omega \to [0, \infty[\] such that the corresponding family of kernels $\rho\gamma$ is a specification.
nodes.label: def:modif

nodes.name: Modifier of a modifier
nodes.statement: {} Modifying a specification $\gamma$ by $\rho_1$ then $\rho_2$ is the same as modifying it by their product.
nodes.label: lem:modif-modif

nodes.name: A modifier of a proper specification is proper
nodes.statement: {} If $\gamma$ is a specification and $\rho$ a modifier of $\gamma$, then $\rho\gamma$ is a proper specification.
nodes.label: lem:modif-proper

nodes.statement: For all $\Lambda \in \mathrm{Finset}(S)$, $A \in \mathcal E^S$, $B \in \mathcal{F}_{S\setminus\Lambda}$, $\eta : S \to E$, we want to prove $$(\rho\gamma)_\Lambda(A \cap B | \eta) = 1_B(\eta) (\rho\gamma)_\Lambda(A B | \eta)$$ Expanding out, this is equivalent to $$\int_{\zeta \in A \cap B} \rho_\Lambda(\zeta)\ d(\gamma_\Lambda(\eta)) = 1_B(\eta) \int_{\zeta \in A} \rho_\Lambda(\zeta)\ d(\gamma_\Lambda(\eta))$$ which is true by Lemma \ref{lem:proper-ker-lintegral} with $f = 1_A\rho_\Lambda$, $g = 1_B$.

nodes.name: Characterisation of modifiers of independent specifications, Proposition 1.30.2
nodes.statement: {} If $\rho$ is a family of measurable densities, $\gamma$ is a proper Markov independent specification, and $\gamma_\Lambda(\rho_\Lambda)=1$ for all $\Lambda$, then TFAE \begin{enumerate} \item $\rho$ is a modifier of $\gamma$ \item For all $\Lambda_1, \Lambda_2$ with $\Lambda_1 \subseteq \Lambda_2$, $\eta : S \to E$ and $\gamma_{\Lambda_2 \setminus \Lambda_1}(\cdot|\alpha)$-almost all $\eta_2 : S \to E$, we have \[\rho_{\Lambda_2}(\zeta_1)\rho_{\Lambda_1}(\zeta_2) = \rho_{\Lambda_2}(\zeta_2) \rho_{\Lambda_1}(\zeta_1)\] for $\gamma_{\Lambda_1}(\cdot|\eta_2) \times \gamma_{\Lambda_1}(\cdot|\eta_2)$-almost all $(\zeta_1, \zeta_2)$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: prop:modif-indep-char

nodes.name: Premodifier, Definition 1.31
nodes.statement: A family of measurable functions $h_\Lambda : (S \to E) \to [0, \infty[$ is a {\bf premodifier} if $$h_{\Lambda_2}(\zeta)h_{\Lambda_1}(\eta) = h_{\Lambda_1}(\zeta)h_{\Lambda_2}(\eta)$$ for all $\Lambda_1 \subseteq \Lambda_2$ and all $\zeta, \eta : S \to E$ such that $\zeta_{\Lambda_1^c} = \eta_{\Lambda_1^c}$.
